chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Fadl ibn Yunus, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
There is neither Hajj nor Umrah upon the owned slave until he is freed.

key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكِ: The owned slave (male or female) in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.حَجٌّ: Hajj, the major annual pilgrimage to Mecca
key_terms.عُمْرَةٌ: Umrah, the minor pilgrimage to Mecca

ai.seo_question: Is Hajj obligatory on a slave before they are freed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the primary obligation (fard) of Hajj and Umrah is suspended for a slave until emancipation, as these rituals require financial independence and the ability to fulfill personal duties. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling distinguishes between the slave's potential to perform Hajj as a recommended act (mandub) with permission, versus the binding obligation which awaits full freedom and solvency. It underscores the principle that Hajj is contingent upon the capacity to bear its costs without neglecting one's own maintenance or obligations to the master.
